title: Cancellation & Refunds
outcome: An authenticated booking owner can request cancellation of an eligible confirmed booking, receive a versioned and explainable refund entitlement, and track the governed cancellation and refund outcome without erasing booking, payment, inventory or audit history.
actor: Authenticated NoorPath booking owner, with authorized operator staff handling governed review and exceptions.
modules: Booking owns cancellation request state, booking lifecycle transitions and the immutable cancellation-policy snapshot used for the decision.
Payments owns refund authorization, provider execution, append-only refund ledger entries and reconciliation state.
Inventory owns release of committed inventory exactly once after an approved booking cancellation.
My Journey consumes customer-safe cancellation and refund projections without deriving financial truth in the web layer.
Operational Support composes cancellation exceptions but may act only through Booking- and Payments-owned commands.
Accounts owns authentication and booking-owner isolation; Operator Access owns permission and operator-scope enforcement.
routes: My Journey -> Booking -> Cancellation and refund status
Operator workspace -> Cancellation case -> Approve or reject
Operational Support -> Cancellation or refund exception
acceptance: The booking owner can view the versioned cancellation policy and an explainable estimated entitlement before submitting a request.
Only an account-owned eligible booking can be requested for cancellation; foreign-account resources return safe not-found responses.
Cancellation requests are idempotent and reject duplicate active requests or invalid booking states.
The entitlement calculation carries explicit currency, policy version, calculation inputs, fee components and the maximum refundable amount derived from authoritative settled-payment facts.
The web client never invents a fee, refund amount, balance or cancellation outcome.
Cancellation request, approval, booking cancellation, inventory release, refund authorization, provider execution and refund settlement remain explicit separate states.
An approved cancellation changes booking state without deleting the booking, commercial snapshot, travellers, payments, documents, visa cases or audit evidence.
Committed inventory is released exactly once through the Inventory-owned command after the approved booking cancellation transition.
Refunds create append-only financial records and never edit or erase original settled payments.
Provider retries, callbacks and reconciliation are idempotent and cannot create duplicate refund facts.
Operator decisions require permission, operator scope, reason, expected version and an auditable actor/timestamp/outcome.
The booking owner can see requested, under-review, approved, rejected, refund-pending, partially-refunded, refunded and failed/recovery-required states using customer-safe language.
Operational exceptions are recoverable through explicit module-owned commands rather than direct state editing.

Every generated or changed page, section, breadcrumb, card, action target and redirect is reachable through its intended clickable navigation on desktop and mobile, or is explicitly recorded as BLOCKED_IDENTITY with the required identity and follow-up verification step.
Direct-route tests supplement but do not replace click-through navigation verification from My Journey, the Operator workspace and Operational Support.
Logs and telemetry use opaque identifiers and exclude payment payloads, traveller data, document data, tokens and provider secrets.
Loading, unavailable, ineligible, stale, duplicate, permission-denied, provider-delayed and recoverable-error states are complete and accessible.
Customer and operator surfaces extend the approved NoorPath visual language and pass keyboard, focus, reflow, target-size, reduced-motion and WCAG checks.
policyDecisionsRequired: The cancellation windows and fee schedule relative to departure date/time, including the governing timezone.
Whether the MVP policy differs by operator, departure or package, and who may publish a policy version.
Which paid components are refundable, non-refundable or capped, including provider fees and already-incurred supplier costs.
Whether customer requests always require operator approval or may auto-approve in explicitly safe windows.
The allowed cancellation cutoff and treatment after material fulfilment milestones such as ticketing, visa submission or visa decision.
The customer-facing refund processing expectation and escalation threshold.
The policy for operator-initiated cancellation, including whether it uses a separate entitlement rule.
exclusions: Partial cancellation of selected travellers within a booking.
Changing occupancy or substituting travellers as part of cancellation.
Chargebacks, disputes, card-network arbitration or fraud case management.
Unrestricted operator editing of refund amounts or historical payment facts.
Automated supplier recovery, airline refund, hotel refund or insurance integrations.
Cancellation of draft quotes, expired inventory holds or unconfirmed checkout attempts already handled by their owning slices.
Promotional credits, vouchers, loyalty points or goodwill compensation.
Production refund execution before provider credentials, legal policy and Product Owner approval are complete.
